source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice mcqs written from Chapter 11 (PDF 251-260), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 11 (Special Theory of Relativity) ke poore chapter se practice MCQs hain, chapter ke sections ki tarteeb mein. Har sawal ka aik sahi jawab hai aur saath mukhtasar wajah; numerical sawalon mein hal ke qadam diye gaye hain.

blocks.prompt:
1 Classical physics based on Newton's laws failed to explain phenomena involving:
(Newton ke qawaneen par mabni classical physics kin phenomena (mazahir) ki wazahat na kar saki?)

options.text: bohat chhote zarraat ya bohat tez raftaar

blocks.explanation: Naye tajurbat ne dikhaya ke classical physics bohat chhote zarraat ya bohat tez raftaar ki wazahat nahi kar sakti (11.1).

book_ref.quote: could not explain phenomena involving extremely small particles or very high velocities

blocks.prompt:
2 Einstein introduced the special theory of relativity in the year:
(Einstein ne special theory of relativity kis saal pesh ki?)
blocks.explanation: Albert Einstein ne Special Theory of Relativity 1905 mein pesh ki (11.1).

book_ref.quote: Albert Einstein's Special Theory of Relativity, introduced in 1905

blocks.prompt:
3 The special theory of relativity resolved the conflicts between classical mechanics and:
(Special theory of relativity ne classical mechanics aur kis theory ke darmiyan tazaad (conflict) door kiya?)
blocks.explanation: Is theory ne classical mechanics aur electromagnetic theory ke darmiyan tazaad door kiya (11.1).

book_ref.quote: resolved the conflicts between classical mechanics and electromagnetic theory

blocks.prompt:
4 A ball thrown to your right appears to move to the left of a person facing you. This shows that direction is:
(Aap ki daayen taraf phenki gayi ball saamne khare shakhs ko baayen taraf jaati nazar aati hai. Is se pata chalta hai ke simt (direction):)

options.text: har observer ke liye aik jaisi

blocks.explanation: Aik ke liye daayen doosre ke liye baayen hai, is liye direction aik nisbati (relative) tasawwur hai (11.1).

book_ref.quote: This illustrates that direction is a relative concept.

blocks.prompt:
5 The walls of a moving train seem stationary to its passengers but moving to a person on the ground. This shows that:
(Chalti train ki deewarein musafiron ko saakin aur zameen par khare shakhs ko harkat mein nazar aati hain. Is se kya sabit hota hai?)

options.text: har harkat observer ke lehaz se (relative) hai

blocks.explanation: Hum yeh nahi keh sakte ke koi jism mutlaq saakin hai ya harkat mein; har harkat observer ya frame ke lehaz se hai (11.1).

book_ref.quote: all motions are relative to the observer or to the reference frame being used

blocks.prompt:
6 A ball is dropped inside a train that is at rest. Its horizontal distance travelled is:
(Saakin train ke andar aik ball giraayi jaati hai. Is ka ufuqi (horizontal) faasla kitna hoga?)
blocks.explanation: Train saakin ho to ball ki horizontal velocity zero hai, is liye horizontal faasla bhi zero hai (11.1, case a).

book_ref.quote: the horizontal velocity of the ball will be zero

blocks.prompt:
7 A ball is dropped in a train moving with uniform velocity. An observer standing outside sees the ball follow a:
(Yaksaan velocity se chalti train mein ball giraayi jaati hai. Bahar khara observer ball ka raasta kaisa dekhta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Ball ke paas train ki horizontal velocity vₒ hoti hai, is liye bahar wale observer ko projectile raasta nazar aata hai (11.1, case b).

book_ref.quote: an observer outside the train will see the ball following a projectile path

blocks.prompt:
8 For an observer inside a train moving with uniform velocity, a dropped ball lands:
(Yaksaan velocity se chalti train ke andar wale observer ke liye giraayi gayi ball kahan girti hai?)

options.text: chhorne wale point ke bilkul neeche

blocks.explanation: Train, observer aur ball sab aik jaisa horizontal faasla vₒt tay karte hain, is liye ball bilkul neeche girti hai (11.1).

book_ref.quote: Therefore, the observer inside the train sees that the ball falls to a point on the floor directly below

blocks.prompt:
9 A train moves with a uniform velocity of 15 m s⁻¹. A ball dropped in it takes 0.4 s to reach the floor. For an observer on the ground, the horizontal distance travelled by the ball is:
(Train 15 m s⁻¹ ki yaksaan velocity se chal rahi hai. Is mein giraayi gayi ball 0.4 s mein farsh tak pohanchti hai. Zameen par khare observer ke liye ball ka horizontal faasla kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: Horizontal faasla = vₒt = 15 × 0.4 = 6.0 m (11.1, case b).

book_ref.quote: It travels a horizontal distance vₒt in time t it takes for the ball to reach the floor.

blocks.prompt:
10 A frame of reference is:
(Frame of reference kya hai?)

options.text: koi bhi coordinate system jis ke lehaz se paimaish ki jaye
aisa frame jo hamesha saakin ho
aisa frame jo hamesha accelerate kare

blocks.explanation: Frame of reference koi bhi coordinate system hai jis ke lehaz se paimaish (measurement) ki jaye (11.2).

book_ref.quote: a frame of reference is any coordinate system relative to which measurements are taken

blocks.prompt:
11 The position of a spaceship is described relative to:
(Spaceship ki position kis ke lehaz se bayan ki jaati hai?)
blocks.explanation: Door ke sitaron par mabni coordinate system spaceship ka frame of reference hai (11.2).

book_ref.quote: The position of a spaceship can be described relative to the positions of distant stars

blocks.prompt:
12 An experiment is performed inside a moving train. The frame of reference for the measurements is:
(Chalti train ke andar aik tajurba kiya jata hai. Paimaish ka frame of reference kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Jab tajurba chalti train mein ho to train hi frame of reference ban jaati hai (11.2).

book_ref.quote: If the same experiment is performed in a moving train, the train becomes the frame of reference

blocks.prompt:
13 A frame of reference in which the law of inertia is valid is called:
(Woh frame of reference jis mein law of inertia (jumood ka qanoon) laagu ho, kya kehlata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Inertial frame aisa coordinate system hai jis mein law of inertia laagu hota hai (11.2).

book_ref.quote: An inertial frame of reference is defined as a coordinate system in which the law of inertia is valid

blocks.prompt:
14 A frame of reference moving with uniform velocity relative to an inertial frame is:
(Inertial frame ke lehaz se yaksaan velocity se chalne wala frame kaisa hai?)
blocks.explanation: Inertial frame ke lehaz se yaksaan velocity wala har frame bhi inertial hai, jaise yaksaan raftaar se chalti car (11.2).

book_ref.quote: any frame of reference moving with uniform velocity relative to an inertial frame is also an inertial frame

blocks.prompt:
15 Which of the following is a non-inertial frame of reference?
(In mein se non-inertial frame of reference kaun sa hai?)

options.text: Inertial frame ke lehaz se yaksaan chalne wala frame

blocks.explanation: Car achanak ruke ya accelerate kare to andar jism saakin nahi rehta; accelerated frame non-inertial hai (11.2).

book_ref.quote: if the moving car is suddenly stopped or accelerated, the body inside no longer remains at rest

blocks.prompt:
16 Strictly, the Earth is a non-inertial frame because it rotates and revolves. It is still treated as an inertial frame because:
(Ghoomne aur gardish ki wajah se Zameen asal mein non-inertial frame hai. Phir bhi use inertial frame kyun maana jata hai?)

options.text: is par law of inertia laagu nahi hota
is ka acceleration nisbatan kam hai

blocks.explanation: Zameen ka acceleration nisbatan bohat kam hai, is liye use aksar inertial frame maana jata hai (11.2).

book_ref.quote: it is often treated as an inertial frame due to its relatively small acceleration

blocks.prompt:
17 Relativity is the study of how:
(Relativity kis cheez ka mutaala hai?)

options.text: harkat karte frames ke observers duniya ko kaise dekhte hain
garam ajsaam roshni kaise banate hain
hararat garam se thande jism ki taraf kaise behti hai

blocks.explanation: Box ke mutabiq relativity is baat ka mutaala hai ke harkat karte frames ke observers duniya ko kaise dekhte hain (11.2).

book_ref.quote: Relativity is the study of the way in which observers from moving frame of reference affect your perception of the world.

blocks.prompt:
18 The special theory of relativity deals with:
(Special theory of relativity kis qisam ke frames se mutaalliq hai?)

options.text: sirf black hole ke qareeb frames

blocks.explanation: Special theory inertial (ghair-accelerating) frames se mutaalliq hai; general theory accelerating frames se (11.3).

book_ref.quote: The special theory of relativity addresses problems involving inertial (non-accelerating) frames of reference.

blocks.prompt:
19 Frames of reference that are accelerating relative to one another are dealt with by:
(Aik doosre ke lehaz se accelerate karne wale frames ka mutaala kis theory mein hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: General theory of relativity aik doosre ke lehaz se accelerate karne wale frames se mutaalliq hai (11.3).

book_ref.quote: that deals with problems involving frames of reference that are accelerating relative to one another

blocks.prompt:
20 The statement "the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames" is called the:
("Physics ke qawaneen tamam inertial frames mein aik jaise hain" is bayan ko kya kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Pehla postulate (mafrooza) Principle of Relativity hai: physics ke qawaneen tamam inertial frames mein aik jaise hain (11.3).

book_ref.quote: The laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames (Principle of Relativity).

blocks.prompt:
21 According to the second postulate, the speed of light in free space:
(Doosre postulate ke mutabiq khala (free space) mein roshni ki speed:)

options.text: tamam observers ke liye aik jaisi hai
source ki harkat par munhasir hai
observer ki harkat par munhasir hai
source ki taraf jaane wale observer ke liye zyada hai

blocks.explanation: Khala mein roshni ki speed tamam observers ke liye aik jaisi hai, source ya observer ki harkat se farq nahi parta (11.3).

book_ref.quote: regardless of the state of motion of the source or the observer (Principle of Constancy of Light)

blocks.prompt:
22 Light from the flashlight of a car moving with speed v is measured by the driver and by a man on the road. Compared with the driver, the man on the road measures its speed as:
(Speed v se chalti car ki flashlight ki roshni ki speed driver aur sarak par khara aadmi naapte hain. Driver ke muqable mein sarak wala aadmi kya naapta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Dono observers car ki roshni ki speed aik hi, yani c, naapte hain (11.3, Do You Know?).

book_ref.quote: is measured same by two observers, one moving in the car with speed v and other standing on the road

blocks.prompt:
23 The first postulate of special relativity implies that:
(Special relativity ke pehle postulate ka nateeja kya hai?)

options.text: mutlaq yaksaan harkat hamesha maloom ki ja sakti hai
mutlaq (absolute) yaksaan harkat maloom nahi ki ja sakti
roshni ki speed source par munhasir hai

blocks.explanation: Agar qawaneen frames mein mukhtalif hote to pata chal jata kaun harkat mein hai; aisa nahi, is liye mutlaq yaksaan harkat maloom nahi ki ja sakti (11.3).

book_ref.quote: implying that there is no way to detect absolute uniform motion

blocks.prompt:
24 The value of the universal constant c used in this chapter is:
(Is chapter mein universal constant c ki qeemat kya li gayi hai?)
blocks.explanation: Khala mein roshni ki speed universal constant hai, c = 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ (11.3).

book_ref.quote: the speed of light in free space is a universal constant, denoted as c

blocks.prompt:
25 Because the speed of light c is constant for all observers:
(Kyunke roshni ki speed c tamam observers ke liye mustaqil hai, is liye:)

options.text: space aur time mutlaq ho jaate hain
mass speed se be-niaz ho jata hai
space aur time nisbati (relative) ho jaate hain
tamam harkat mutlaq ho jaati hai

blocks.explanation: Kyunke c mustaqil hai, is liye space aur time nisbati (relative) ho jaate hain (11.3).

book_ref.quote: Since c is constant, space and time become relative.

blocks.prompt:
26 A person in a train moving at constant velocity close to the speed of light holds a mirror at arm's length. The person:
(Roshni ki speed ke qareeb mustaqil velocity se chalti train mein aik shakhs baazu ke faasle par aaina pakarta hai. Woh shakhs:)

options.text: apna aks aam tarah dekhta hai
aks kuch second der se dekhta hai

blocks.explanation: Koi tajurba train ki mustaqil harkat ko andar wale shakhs ke lehaz se maloom nahi kar sakta, is liye woh apna aks aam tarah dekhta hai (11.3; book correction: train c par nahi, mustaqil velocity se chalti hai).

book_ref.quote: no experiment can detect the constant motion of the train relative to the person inside it

blocks.prompt:
27 Two consequences of the postulates of special relativity, as seen by a stationary observer, are:
(Saakin observer ke lehaz se special relativity ke postulates ke do nataaij kya hain?)

options.text: harkat karti ghariyan aahista aur lambaiyan chhoti
har frame mein waqt aur lambai mustaqil

blocks.explanation: Postulates ka nateeja: saakin observer ko harkat karte frames ki ghariyan aahista aur lambaiyan chhoti nazar aati hain (11.3).

book_ref.quote: the slowing down of clocks and the contraction of lengths in moving reference frames

blocks.prompt:
28 According to the special theory of relativity, time:
(Special theory of relativity ke mutabiq waqt (time):)

options.text: tamam observers ke liye aik jaisa hai
sirf ghari ke mass par munhasir hai
frame of reference ki harkat par munhasir hai

blocks.explanation: Waqt mutlaq miqdaar nahi; yeh frame of reference ki harkat par munhasir hai (11.3).

book_ref.quote: time is not an absolute quantity; it depends on the motion of the frame of reference

blocks.prompt:
29 The time interval between two events measured by an observer at rest in the frame of the events is called:
(Events ke frame mein saakin observer jo do events ka darmiyani waqt naapta hai, use kya kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Events ke frame mein saakin observer ka naapa hua waqfa tₒ proper time kehlata hai (11.3).

book_ref.quote: This is known as proper time.

blocks.prompt:
30 In the relation t = tₒ/√(1 − v²/c²), the time t measured by a moving observer is:
(t = tₒ/√(1 − v²/c²) mein harkat karte observer ka naapa hua waqt t:)
blocks.explanation: √(1 − v²/c²) hamesha aik se kam hai, is liye t, tₒ se zyada hai: waqt phail gaya (dilate hua) (11.3).

book_ref.quote: is always less than one, so t is greater than

blocks.prompt:
31 Time dilation applies to:
(Time dilation kin processes par laagu hota hai?)

options.text: tamam processes: physical, chemical aur biological

blocks.explanation: Time dilation tamam waqt naapne wale processes par laagu hai, physical, chemical aur biological; budhapa bhi aahista hota hai (11.3).

book_ref.quote: This astonishing result applies to all timing processes

blocks.prompt:
32 A clock ticks once every 2.0 s in its own frame. What interval between ticks is measured by an observer moving at 0.6 c relative to the clock?
(Aik ghari apne frame mein har 2.0 s baad tick karti hai. Ghari ke lehaz se 0.6 c se chalne wala observer ticks ka darmiyani waqfa kitna naapega?)

book_ref.quote: the time measured by the observer will not be

blocks.prompt:
33 An event takes 10 s as measured by a traveler in a spaceship moving at 0.8 c. For an observer outside, the same event takes:
(0.8 c se chalte spaceship mein musafir ke mutabiq aik event 10 s leta hai. Bahar ke observer ke liye yahi event kitna waqt leta hai?)

book_ref.quote: the event takes one second as measured by the traveler

blocks.prompt:
34 An observer finds that a process in a frame moving past him at 0.6 c lasts 5.0 s. The proper time of the process is:
(Observer dekhta hai ke us ke paas se 0.6 c se guzarte frame mein aik process 5.0 s chalta hai. Process ka proper time kitna hai?)

book_ref.quote: if the frame of events is moving with respect to the observer with a uniform relativistic velocity v

blocks.prompt:
35 At relativistic speeds, the aging process of the human body, as seen by a stationary observer:
(Relativistic speeds par insani jism ka budhapa (aging), saakin observer ke lehaz se:)
blocks.explanation: Time dilation biological processes par bhi laagu hai, is liye bohat tez raftaar par budhapa aahista hota hai (11.3).

book_ref.quote: Even the aging process of the human body is slowed by motion at very high speeds

blocks.prompt:
36 Compared with an observer on the Earth, an observer in a fast moving spaceship measures the distance from Earth to a star:
(Zameen wale observer ke muqable mein tez spaceship ka observer Zameen se sitare tak faasla kaisa naapta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Harkat karte spaceship ke observer ko faasla chhota nazar aata hai; yeh length contraction hai (11.3).

book_ref.quote: would appear smaller than the distance measured by an observer on the Earth

blocks.prompt:
37 Length contraction occurs:
(Length contraction kis rukh mein hota hai?)

options.text: sirf harkat ke amoodi rukh mein

blocks.explanation: Length contraction sirf harkat ke rukh mein hota hai; amoodi rukh mein nahi (11.3).

book_ref.quote: Length contraction occurs only along the direction of motion

blocks.prompt:
38 A rod of length 1.0 m is held perpendicular to the direction of motion of a spaceship moving at 0.8 c. Its length measured by an observer at rest outside is:
(1.0 m lamba rod 0.8 c se chalte spaceship mein harkat ke amoodi (perpendicular) rakha hai. Bahar saakin observer us ki lambai kitni naapega?)
blocks.explanation: Harkat ke amoodi rukh mein koi contraction nahi hota, is liye lambai 1.0 m hi rahegi (11.3).

book_ref.quote: no such contraction is observed perpendicular to the direction of motion

blocks.prompt:
39 The length of an object measured by an observer at rest relative to it is called:
(Kisi jism ke lehaz se saakin observer us ki jo lambai naapta hai, use kya kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Jism ke lehaz se saakin observer ki naapi hui lambai proper length ℓₒ kehlati hai (11.3).

book_ref.quote: is called the proper length

blocks.prompt:
40 A rod 2.0 m long at rest moves along its length at 0.6 c relative to an observer. The observer measures its length as:
(Saakin halat mein 2.0 m lamba rod apni lambai ke rukh mein observer ke lehaz se 0.6 c se chalta hai. Observer us ki lambai kitni naapega?)

book_ref.quote: If an object and an observer are in relative motion with speed v

blocks.prompt:
41 A spaceship is 50 m long at rest. It moves at 0.8 c. A person inside the spaceship measures its length as:
(Aik spaceship saakin halat mein 50 m lamba hai. Yeh 0.8 c se chalta hai. Spaceship ke andar wala shakhs us ki lambai kitni naapega?)
blocks.explanation: Andar wala shakhs spaceship ke lehaz se saakin hai, is liye woh proper length 50 m naapta hai (11.3). Bahar wala 50 × 0.6 = 30 m naapega.

book_ref.quote: A person inside the train will measure its length as 100 metres.

blocks.prompt:
42 A spaceship is 50 m long at rest. It flies past an observer at 0.8 c. The observer measures its length as:
(Aik spaceship saakin halat mein 50 m lamba hai. Yeh observer ke paas se 0.8 c se guzarta hai. Observer us ki lambai kitni naapega?)

book_ref.quote: a person standing by the side of the track will observe the train to be only 60 metres long

blocks.prompt:
43 At what speed will a rod moving along its length appear to an observer at rest to be half of its proper length?
(Apni lambai ke rukh mein chalta rod kis speed par saakin observer ko apni proper length ka aadha nazar aayega?)
blocks.explanation: ℓ/ℓₒ = √(1 − v²/c²) = 0.5, is liye v²/c² = 0.75 aur v = 0.866 c (11.3).

book_ref.quote: This effect is known as length contraction.

blocks.prompt:
44 According to the special theory of relativity, the mass of an object:
(Special theory of relativity ke mutabiq kisi jism ka mass:)

options.text: is ki speed par munhasir hai
speed barhne se kam hota hai

blocks.explanation: Mass aik badalne wali miqdaar hai jo jism ki speed par munhasir hai (11.3).

book_ref.quote: the mass of an object is a variable quantity that depends on the object's speed

blocks.prompt:
45 The increase in the mass of an object at high speed indicates an increase in its:
(Tez raftaar par jism ke mass ka barhna us ki kis cheez mein izafa zahir karta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Mass ka barhna inertia (jumood) mein izafa hai; speed badalne ke liye zyada force chahiye (11.3).

book_ref.quote: The increase in mass indicates the increase in inertia that an object has at high speeds.

blocks.prompt:
46 A material object cannot be accelerated to the speed of light because, as v approaches c, its mass:
(Koi maaddi jism roshni ki speed tak accelerate nahi ho sakta kyunke jab v, c ke qareeb jaye to us ka mass:)

options.text: rest mass ke barabar rehta hai
rest mass ka aadha ho jata hai

blocks.explanation: Jab v → c, √(1 − v²/c²) → 0 aur m → ∞; la-mehdood mass ke liye la-mehdood force chahiye jo maujood nahi (11.3).

book_ref.quote: An infinite mass would require an infinite force to accelerate it.

blocks.prompt:
47 A body has a rest mass of 2.0 kg. Its mass when moving at 0.6 c is:
(Aik jism ka rest mass 2.0 kg hai. 0.6 c se chalte waqt us ka mass kitna hoga?)

book_ref.quote: An object whose mass is measured at rest is called its rest mass

blocks.prompt:
48 At what speed does the mass of a particle become twice its rest mass?
(Kis speed par kisi zarre ka mass us ke rest mass ka dugna ho jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: m/mₒ = 2 ka matlab √(1 − v²/c²) = 0.5, is liye v²/c² = 0.75 aur v = 0.866 c (11.3).

book_ref.quote: will have an increased mass m when observed to be moving at speed v

blocks.prompt:
49 The ratio m/mₒ for a body moving at 0.28 c is about:
(0.28 c se chalte jism ke liye m/mₒ ki nisbat taqreeban kitni hai?)

book_ref.quote: As v approaches c, it requires a greater force to change the object's speed.

blocks.prompt:
50 Newton's laws are valid in everyday situations because everyday speeds are:
(Rozmarra zindagi mein Newton ke qawaneen kyun durust hain? Kyunke rozmarra speeds:)

options.text: roshni ki speed ke muqable mein bohat kam

blocks.explanation: Zameen ki orbital speed (30 km s⁻¹) bhi 300,000 km s⁻¹ ke muqable mein bohat kam hai, is liye Newton ke qawaneen chalte hain (11.3).

book_ref.quote: This is why Newton's laws are valid in everyday situations.

blocks.prompt:
51 Using the chapter's values, Earth's orbital speed (30 km s⁻¹) is what fraction of the speed of light in free space (300,000 km s⁻¹)?
(Chapter ki qeematon se Zameen ki orbital speed (30 km s⁻¹) khala mein roshni ki speed (300,000 km s⁻¹) ka kitna hissa hai?)
blocks.explanation: 30/300,000 = 1 × 10⁻⁴, is liye relativistic asraat na hone ke barabar hain; yeh sirf roshni ki speed ke qareeb numayan hote hain (11.3).

book_ref.quote: relativistic effects become very prominent

blocks.prompt:
52 Whether two events at different places are simultaneous:
(Mukhtalif jagahon par do events aik hi waqt (simultaneous) hue ya nahi, yeh:)

options.text: tamam observers ke liye aik jaisa hai
sirf un ke darmiyan faasle par munhasir hai
observer ke frame of reference par munhasir hai
observer ke mass par munhasir hai

blocks.explanation: Aik observer ke liye simultaneous events doosre harkat karte frame ke observer ke liye aam tor par simultaneous nahi hote (11.3).

book_ref.quote: whether two events are seen as simultaneous depends on the observer's frame of reference

blocks.prompt:
53 In a train with light-operated doors, a traveler in the middle switches on the light. The traveler sees the two doors open:
(Roshni se khulne wale darwazon wali train mein darmiyan khara musafir light jalata hai. Musafir dono darwaze kaise khulte dekhta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Roshni aage peechhe barabar speed se jaati aur dono darwazon tak saath pohanchti hai, is liye musafir dono ko aik saath khulte dekhta hai (11.3).

book_ref.quote: the traveler sees both doors opening simultaneously

blocks.prompt:
54 In the same light-operated door experiment, an observer outside the moving train sees:
(Isi tajurbe mein chalti train ke bahar wala observer kya dekhta hai?)

options.text: agla darwaza pichhle se pehle khulta hai
pichhla darwaza agle se pehle khulta hai

blocks.explanation: Pichhla darwaza roshni ki taraf aur agla door ja raha hai, is liye bahar wala pehle pichhla darwaza khulta dekhta hai (11.3).

book_ref.quote: an observer outside the train will see the back door open before the front door

blocks.prompt:
55 In a frame moving at constant velocity from which no other frame can be seen, you:
(Mustaqil velocity se chalte aise frame mein jahan se koi aur frame nazar na aaye, aap:)

options.text: hamesha jaan sakte hain ke harkat mein hain
nahi jaan sakte ke harkat mein hain ya saakin
pendulum se apni speed jaan sakte hain
ball gira kar jaan sakte hain ke saakin hain

blocks.explanation: Aise frame mein yeh jaanne ka koi tareeqa nahi ke aap harkat mein hain ya saakin (11.3, Interesting Information).

book_ref.quote: there is no way to know if you are moving or at rest

blocks.text: 11.4 The equivalence between mass and energy

blocks.prompt:
56 According to the special theory of relativity, mass and energy are:
(Special theory of relativity ke mutabiq mass aur energy:)

options.text: alag magar aik doosre mein badalne ke qaabil
aik hi cheez aur kabhi nahi badalte

blocks.explanation: Mass aur energy alag cheezein hain magar aik doosre mein badal sakti hain, E = mc² ke zariye (11.4).
